prompt:
Create an illustrated science-fiction world with convincing three-dimensional depth and a hand-inked graphic-novel finish. Use strong silhouettes, expressive outlines, textured shadows and worn materials. Build environments from layered machinery, exposed pipes, suspended cables, overlapping panels and objects that suggest everyday use and repair. Organize dense detail around clear focal points. Use controlled colour palettes with warm luminous accents against cool shadow, giving each location its own atmosphere. The world should feel active, inhabited and larger than the visible frame, with layered depth, while the composition stays clear. Overall: lived-in, cyber, illustrated science fiction, lit and readable: warm lamplight against cool blue-steel shadow, dark only in the corners. This is a still picture and code adds the motion, so paint everything crisply: no motion blur, no lens blur, no film grain.

Room A, the crew bay, in the same illustrated world: blue steel, lit warm. The whole room is one blue-steel family, the colours of the attached guide: deep navy in the shadows and corners (#14243F, #1D3D6B), steel blue on the walls and the deck (#2D609E), turning paler where the light falls (#5C92CC, #A9CAEB). The light is warm: the two light bars glow cream along their length (#FCE3A0), with a warm paper-white glow (#F4EBDD) on the ceiling around them and soft pools of pale light on the deck below. Walls, panels, pipes, cables and deck plates take their colour from that family; worn edges, rivets and plate seams show a little rust (#75402E); nothing is neutral grey, and nothing is tan, beige, olive, purple or violet. The shadows are deep navy, never black-brown or grey. Labels and paper are blank, in a warm paper white (#F4EBDD). Small indicator lights are warm orange (#EC793C); no other coloured light, and no green, purple or red light. Practical and worn, a working bay, quiet but lived in. The guide is the room's colour plan: paint over it in full detail and texture, but keep its colours and where its light falls.

The room: Room A, the crew bay, a 4 m square room with a 3 m ceiling, here with no furniture in it. The ceiling is solid steel panels, with no skylight and no opening in it: two long light bars set into it run across the room about 1.4 m apart, each glowing warm cream along its whole length behind a plain diffuser, lighting the ceiling around it and throwing soft pools of light on the deck below. The walls are steel panels, pipes, conduits, cable runs and small lockers, worn and repaired, darker toward the deck, with a narrow rust-brown kick strip along their foot; the deck is metal plates with seams, scuffs and a little rust, lit pale under the light bars and darker toward the corners. No beams, rays or shafts of light in the air.

View: a straight-lined view at standing eye height, exactly as the attached guide shows: 80 degrees across and level, every vertical line perfectly straight and upright, every straight line in the room straight in the picture. The horizon, at eye level, is a straight line 714 px from the top, a little above the middle. Match the guide's layout, perspective, horizon and proportions exactly, line for line, as its floor seams, wall bases, corners and ceiling edges show. Do not curve the lines, tilt the view, zoom in or out, or move the horizon.

This picture: from a place by the north wall, west of its middle, at standing eye height, looking diagonally across the room toward its south-east corner, which stands right of the middle. Ahead and on the left, the east wall; on the right, past the corner, the south wall. Above, the solid ceiling, with the two light bars running from its middle up to the right and out of the picture at its top and right edges, the nearer one higher. The deck is open and clear, with nothing standing on it, while the walls keep their pipes, panels and conduits.

No people, and no words, letters or logos. Leave screens plain for the game to fill: openings marked black in the guide stay flat black and empty. No figures, faces, hands, silhouettes or animals; no signs, symbols or readable screens (any label is blank or abstract marks); no buttons or panels that look like game controls; no emblems, insignia, signature, watermark or border.
